svg.text: Keeping key order: what moves on an insertion or a deletion
A conventional node keeps descriptors sorted and shifts them to open or close a gap. The tree keeps descriptors in fixed slots and shifts only the one-byte slot indices of order[].
Leaf descriptor, 64-bit build: RangeRef 24 B + cv 8 B = 32 B. Capacity 8 here; real capacity follows the block size. Highlighted cells are the bytes written or moved by the operation.
same six entries, in arbitrary slots; order[] gives the sorted sequence, a set free bit an empty slot
Insert coconut (rank 3, between cherry and date)
shift date, fig, grape one slot right: 3 descriptors × 32 B = 96 B moved, then write 32 B
write the descriptor into free slot 3 (32 B), clear free bit 3, shift three order bytes: 3 B moved
shift cherry … grape one slot left: 5 descriptors × 32 B = 160 B moved
set free bit 4 and shift five order bytes: 5 B moved; the descriptor is left in place and the slot is reusable
In a leaf of 59 entries, an insertion or deletion in the middle shifts about 29 bytes of order[] instead of about 29 × 32 B ≈ 930 B of descriptors. A logical
internal entry (24 B RangeRef, one child pointer and two CVs: 48 B on 64-bit, excluding order[] and node metadata) is larger still. Both designs write the
new descriptor itself. Reading pays one indirection (order[rank] → slot), parentRank() scans order[] to recover a rank, and splits still move descriptors
between nodes. Physical slots never change while an entry lives in a node, which is what keeps parentSlot references valid across reorderings.
